## 0. Role, authority, and honesty

Design reproducible, editable, publication-quality Microsoft PowerPoint presentations containing complex scientific diagrams, mathematical notation, original icons, data-linked charts, diagrams revealed by click, and appropriately limited spatial animations. Preserve the meaning and provenance of every object.

Before any scientific drafting, inspect current repository authorities in their binding order:
1. `AI_RESEARCH_INSTRUCTIONS.md` and `project/CURRENT_THESIS_AUTHORITY_INDEX_V1.md`.
2. `project/CANONICAL_EVIDENCE_NON_INVENTION_STANDARD_V1.md` and `thesis/00_governance/THESIS_CITATION_AND_REFERENCE_STANDARD_V1.md`.
3. Exact frozen thesis title, complete P/T_e scope, extreme-heat-only thermally conditioned interdependencies, state-time, resilience, sustainability, objectives and applicable decision protocol.
4. Existing Deck3 SKILL.md, DECK3_SRGB_PALETTE.json, WORKFLOW.md, comparative lessons and scientific-diagram/infographic/mathematical visualization skills.

Never treat this skill as scientific source authority, a proven model, a sanctioned new objective, or permission to invent measurements, thermal transfer equations, real asset geometry, parameters, thresholds, empirical fit, bidirectional coupling or novelty. Cite each external scientific claim directly next to the claim. Mark unverified case objects OPEN; mark original, explicitly hypothetical derivations T1.

**Release semantics** (never conflate): `SPECIFIED`, `BUILT`, `FILE_VERIFIED`, `RENDER_INSPECTED`, `ANIMATION_IMPORT_VERIFIED`, `POWERPOINT_PLAYBACK_VERIFIED`, `SCIENTIFICALLY_EVIDENCED`, `PHYSICALLY_VALIDATED`. A built effect is not a tested effect; an animated physical mechanism is not a physical proof.

## 1. Invocation and boundaries

Commands (proposed new verbs within Deck3, retaining old three-stage semantics):
- `Deck3 design-audit` — slide-by-slide hierarchy, figure/geometry, scope, citations, projected legibility, QA report; no modifications.
- `Deck3 native-shapes [slide N]` — scientifically defined native PowerPoint objects and stable identifiers.
- `Deck3 vector-icons [slide N]` — research-specific icons as legal original SVG/native vector components.
- `Deck3 curved-arrows [slide N]` — static/connected Bézier and elbow arrows with explicit relation semantics.
- `Deck3 math [slide N]` — equation register, units, mathematically correct native Office Math or SVG fallback.
- `Deck3 animate [slide N|priority|all]` — presenter-controlled animation compiled from an approved click manifest.
- `Deck3 morph [slide N]` — slide-to-slide matched-object transformation when change of view is warranted.
- `Deck3 chart [slide N]` — provenance-backed accessible plots or genuinely synthetic labeled demos.
- `Deck3 accessibility` — alt text, logical reading order, color contrast, motion reduction and text alternatives.
- `Deck3 playback-QA` — run imported effects, reveal-by-reveal screenshots and native Microsoft PowerPoint slide-show acceptance where available.
- `Deck3 export` — editable PPTX, scalable SVG/PDF as supported, bounded PNG preview and build fallback.
- `Deck3 advanced all` — execute only steps requested and those necessary for requested outputs; stop at verified gates.

Stage 1 creates and freezes native textual content and genuinely blank dominant figure regions. Stage 2 makes original science figures and object/reveal manifests. Stage 3 composes without unapproved text mutation. Advanced animation is a separate **Stage 4**, not a backdoor for changing Stage 1.

## 2. Output selection — 12 engineering routes

Always select the **least complex method with verified capabilities** for the task:

| Route | Use when | Strength | Restrictions / fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| Microsoft PowerPoint GUI | One-off complex design, native effects, interactive preview | Strongest visual control | Real desktop software needed; manual repeatability limited |
| `python-pptx` | Declarative layout, editable shapes/text, tables/charts | Easy automated QA | Does not offer comprehensive high-level animation authoring; use separate backend |
| PptxGenJS | JS web/service-driven slide masters and charts | Modern programmatic authoring | Animations not guaranteed; official project wiki lists them unimplemented; verify exact installed release |
| Aspose.Slides | Programmatic native effect/timing/trigger paths | Dedicated animation and motion-path APIs | Licence may apply; independently verify export/playback |
| PowerPoint COM/VBA | Desktop Windows-native automation / effects | PowerPoint-owned object model | Windows-dependent; macros/security/deployment risks; keep output standard PPTX if possible |
| OOXML/DrawingML | Precise technical effect or geometry not exposed elsewhere | Native low-level specification | Must validate timing XML, references and file repair across versions; implementation untrusted until tested |
| SVG-original graphics | Exact scalable machinery, symbols, arrows, mathematical figures | Sharp at any zoom | Inserted SVG may be one unit; convert to shapes only after inspection |
| Office Math / OMML | Editable equations, indices, integrals, operators, matrices | Native semantic math | Office-supported LaTeX subset only; visual/math round-trip QA |
| Morph | Geometric transformation or reconfiguration between slides | Smooth contextual continuity | Slide-to-slide, not same-slide click effect; not a substitute for empirical dynamics |
| Progressive slide build | Guaranteed click-through step sequence | Broad compatibility and static QA | More pages; preserve original page cross-references and source notes |
| PNG/video/GIF | Source-backed raster results or precomputed temporal signal | Reliable visual media delivery | Pixels/frames not independently editable; no false implication of observed data |
| 3D models | Verified spatial/physical object geometry | Useful orientation/assembly explanation | Authentic source/model license, device support, object-level applicability must be checked |

Detailed criteria in `references/ROUTES_AND_MICROSKILLS.md`. Do not claim route support from marketing claims alone; exercise an actual API call and PowerPoint import where possible.

## 3. Minimum required scientific object model

Every scientific graphic/reveal must be grounded in a structured object registry before rendering:

```yaml
slide: 5
scientific_question: "Which directional thermal pathways can be independently qualified?"
view: mechanism
objects:
  - id: s05.p.thermal_state
    class: candidate_physical_state
    parent_system: P
    label: "Power-side thermal state"
    evidence: OPEN
    editable: true
  - id: s05.te.evse.ac_input
    class: interface_electrical_quantity
    parent_system: T_e
    label: "Grid-side AC input"
    evidence: OPEN
relations:
  - id: s05.p_to_te.candidate
    from: s05.p.thermal_state
    to: s05.te.evse.ac_input
    phenomenon: "Conditional mechanism to be qualified; not necessarily direct transfer"
    relation_type: candidate_dependency
    direction: P_to_Te
    evidence: OPEN
    arrow_shape: solid_connector
animations:
  - order: 1
    name: "Source condition"
    object_ids: [s05.p.thermal_state]
    effect: Appear
    trigger: OnClick
    persist: true
```

In actual mechanism diagrams, define physically valid **intermediate objects** instead of drawing a direct arrow between the sample endpoints above. The structure is illustrative schema, **not** a scientifically qualified claim or admissible case model.

For each object, store: unique ID, semantic role, system membership, state/flow/constraint/service distinction, source record, visual geometry, exact authored color token, editability, animation group and accessible explanation. Each relation additionally needs endpoints, direction, physical/methodological meaning, evidence status, arrow type and cited support.

## 4. Scientific diagram grammar

**Scope:** distinct Power System P and complete Electrified Transportation T_e. EVSE, physical charging connection, necessary power-transfer communication and control, circuits, RESS, electrically propelled road vehicles, propulsion and auxiliaries belong to T_e. A selected reduced case is not a new full-system definition. External extreme heat is forcing, not an internal system state.

**Arrow style describes type, NEVER evidence:**
- Solid large directional connector: evidence-qualified or clearly *candidate-labeled* physical quantity/transfer path.
- Dashed connector: declared command/control response where it is causally appropriate.
- Dotted line: observation, sensor/information mapping, not physical power exchange.
- Orthogonal/elbow: topology or orderly routing when topology matters.
- Curved/Bézier: routing around content or a well-defined loop/feedback path; curvature does not assert nonlinear governing dynamics.
- No arrow: containment, category membership, alignment, correspondence or shared external forcing comparison, unless a real directional relation exists.
- For candidate P→T_e and T_e→P thermal pathways, expose each direction independently and keep evidence gating explicit in the scientific record/visible wording where necessary. DC charger output alone does not demonstrate grid-side AC input behavior or subsequent P thermal response.

**Independent forcing fixture:** two lanes from external extreme heat to P/T_e own thermal states. No unqualified cross-system link. **State-service fixture:** thermal state → conditional capability → actual electrical exchange/operation → declared electricity or mobility service → bounded resilience and sustainability interpretation. A thermal threshold is not a demonstrated operating constraint without case evidence.

## 5. Native vector shapes, symbols and icons

Priority: native shapes for primary systems/arrows > original SVG for reusable physical icons > sourced photos only for real equipment or authentic environments > high-resolution PNG for raster-dependent outputs.

Create symbols using documented visual primitives rather than invented equipment silhouette. Set semantic role and source asset record. Build a small icon library with names such as `transformer_generic`, `power_bus`, `evse_generic`, `road_vehicle_generic`, `ress_generic`, `sensor_generic`, `thermal_state`, `service_meter`, `evidence_gate`. These are **illustrative icons**, not manufacturer engineering drawings. All boxes and graphic canvases pure white. Shapes may use approved border/line colors only; no tinted fills, drop shadows, gradients or decorative glows. Avoid emoji icon fonts in scientific diagrams.

Use connectors attached to shape connection points when topology must survive rearrangement. Use `Merge Shapes` (Union, Intersect, Fragment, Subtract, Combine) for native bespoke scientific symbols when the resulting topology is correct. SVGs must have a valid `viewBox`, intrinsic bounds without excessive whitespace and `title`/description or an external alt-text record.

## 6. Curved arrows and mathematical geometry

For a cubic Bézier curve on a diagram:

`B(t)=(1-t)^3 P0+3(1-t)^2 t P1+3(1-t)t^2 P2+t^3 P3` for `0<=t<=1`.

Endpoint tangent `B'(1)=3(P3-P2)`. Choose arrowhead angle `atan2(P3_y-P2_y, P3_x-P2_x)` in **screen coordinates** (y grows downward). Normalize arrowhead direction and reject zero-length tangent. Check endpoint lands at the declared target connection site, does not cross hidden/forbidden nodes and maintains a comfortable label clearance. For multi-segment curves check segment continuity; if C1 smoothness is intended, end/start tangents must be collinear and consistently oriented. For feedback loops, require evidence that the return path actually represents the specified mechanism; not merely two arrows drawn between systems.

**Mathematical verification:** independent Python analytical checker computes endpoints, tangent angles, finite-coordinate assertions and object/line collision boundaries. **Semantic verification:** separately confirm physical relationship type; no geometric test can prove causality. Code/QA example in `examples/geometry_and_manifest_qa.py`.

## 7. Mathematical objects and scientific plots

Create an equation register containing: exact LaTeX/UnicodeMath source, semantic variables, units, assumptions, provenance (A1–A5, T1, OPEN), transformation steps and a screenshot/PNG of the final rendered math for comparison. Prefer Office Math (OMML) when editability matters, using the supported LaTeX subset. SVG/PDF vector source is acceptable when native rendering is not faithful, but state that individual glyph editability is reduced. Never silently replace variables, collapse multiplications, drop subscripts or alter signs.

**Units:** formal test per equation (e.g. `[C_th dT/dt]=J/s=W`; `[(T-T_a)/R_th]=K/(K/W)=W`). The generic lumped thermal balance is a didactic illustration, not an equipment-admitted transformer or EVSE law. State assumptions and limits in slide notes and wherever a figure's claim depends on them.

Scientific charts require: real provenance OR explicitly labeled synthetic data, dimensioned axes/units, assumptions, a meaningful comparator when interpreting changes, event definitions, uncertainty when required and no fake future validated results. Prefer native chart series for editable simple plots; embed original numerical script and CSV/JSON for code-generated vector plots. Avoid animation of empirical trajectories if it implies timing that was not measured or solved.

## 8. Native animation contract

**Default research presentation setting:** `Appear`, `On Click`, previous content **persists**. Each click reveals **one defensible explanatory group** rather than every primitive stroke individually. Static title, claim, approved supporting points, citation/source footer and frozen objective text remain visible from slide start.

Each group has exact IDs, intended order, object membership, relation meaning, trigger, animation API, persistence and verification status. Shapes in a group may be co-timed (first `OnClick`, rest `WithPrevious`) or grouped as one object. Grouping can change existing animations; apply animation **after** grouping and verify stable object IDs and reading order. Use default no sound, no exit effect, no auto-advance; simple effects are preferred. Require keyboard/presenter remote advancement. An evidence gate must not appear after a claim in a way that falsely presents it as validated in earlier frames; preface candidate pathways or keep candidate attribution visible throughout.

**Six priority Chapter 1 animations**: slides 3,4,5,9,10,12 with click groups 3,4,4,4,5,6 respectively (total 26). Optional 7,8,11,13 remain static unless explicitly enabled; static 1,2,6,14–16. See `references/CHAPTER1_ANIMATION_MAP.md`.

**What is truly supported:** Native desktop PowerPoint can author/reorder entrance effects and user triggers. Aspose.Slides exposes `slide.timeline.main_sequence.add_effect(target, EffectType.*, EffectSubtype.*, EffectTriggerType.ON_CLICK)`. `python-pptx` and PptxGenJS should be treated as geometry/authoring layers unless exact-version animation capability is proven. OOXML direct animation edits are an optional specialized backend, requiring strict native importer round-trips. Animations in flattened PNG are whole-image, not independently revealing its internal subparts.

**Morph is separate:** matched objects on consecutive slides, optionally named `!!StableSemanticID` to enforce matching; not the same as an entrance reveal on one slide. Motion paths move *objects*, not energy or heat physically; use only for a clearly specified illustrative object-state transformation, not to assert physical propagation. An animated flow marker must be labeled as conceptual unless data-backed timing is admitted.

Typography: one academic hierarchy, Times New Roman for native scientific slide copy, readable font sizes assessed on a real projected slide, not only close-up. Do not display template metadata `MAIN MESSAGE`/`THREE KEY POINTS`. Display actual message and up to three meaningful supporting points as applicable, exact frozen objectives verbatim, and adjacent author-date citations for externally supported claims. Font substitution must be disclosed; never package font binaries.

Dominant scientific figure: eligible slides target **75% meaningful scientific visual occupancy in the defined usable content region U**, acceptable 70–80% under current Deck3 contract. Content visible bounds `V` must reflect actual meaningful artwork, not a large padded PNG rectangle. Freeze U, V, achieved effective occupancy and exception reasons. Some full-objective/references/title/outline slides are documented exceptions. When exact approved text cannot fit the complementary rail legibly, BLOCK: propose approval for splitting or re-layout rather than shrinking/truncating.

## 10. Accessibility and interaction

Every meaningful visual group must have a descriptive alt-text equivalent, correct screen reader reading order, sufficiently distinct line pattern/marker beyond color, accessible contrast (standard body text >=4.5:1 and essential graphics >=3:1 on white), keyboard/presenter controlled reveals, no essential content visible only in animation, and a static/click-through alternative. Beware that grouping animations after applying effects may remove effects; rebuild them from the manifest and re-check.

For accessibility and no-motion fallback, export the final cumulative state as a static single-slide view and/or exact progressive slides without special effects. Hyperlinks should have descriptive names and must not substitute for embedded source attribution. Avoid fast repetitive motion, automatic loops and distracting 3D rotation. User-facing notes should explain click order without claiming experimental results.

## 11. Testing and release gates

A valid PPTX ZIP file is necessary but **not enough**. Mandatory gates:

- **G0 Input authority:** approved source PPTX/manifest identified, frozen objects and original hashes recorded.
- **G1 Claim & evidence:** citation-to-claim and state/forcing/capability/service boundaries correct; directional causal paths independently qualified or clearly OPEN.
- **G2 Layout/editability:** full editable text, correct colors, white backgrounds, 75% meaningful figure occupancy (or documented exception), readable scaled labels, object alt descriptions.
- **G3 Geometry:** all arrows have valid endpoints/tangents, no lost connected objects, no unexplained crossings or cropped labels.
- **G4 Mathematical:** checked notation/units/provenance; no unverified dataset, parameter, threshold or law silently inserted.
- **G5 Build/OOXML:** save, reopen, archive integrity, correct slide count, stable object IDs, no accidental image flattening.
- **G6 Static presentation:** render every slide and all cumulative reveal frames; compare screenshots, detect clipping/overlap, inspect at actual projection size.
- **G7 Animation importer:** independent importer detects correct count, ordering, `OnClick`, and persistence. Import confirmation does not certify native PowerPoint playback.
- **G8 Native PowerPoint playback:** user/device tests with click, Space/right-arrow, presenter remote, back navigation, show restart, slide order; `POWERPOINT_PLAYBACK_VERIFIED` ONLY after this passes.
- **G9 Accessibility/source release:** screen-reader reading order/contrast/alt text, source metadata, reproducible project files, fallback deck, QA JSON and explicit scientific uncertainty statement.

A failed gate blocks the specific requested release; report precise blocker and a safe fallback instead of claiming completion. Run reproducible unit tests and announce which checks were *executed*, which are only specified, and which require Microsoft PowerPoint GUI. See `references/ACCEPTANCE_AND_TESTS.md`.

## 12. Reference implementation architecture

- `manifest.json`: source, slide, frozen strings, citations, baseline notes/text hashes, U/V geometry, exceptions.
- `objects.json`: names, class, membership, source, geometry, colors, semantic relation, accessible alt.
- `animation_plan.json`: slide, ordered click groups, object IDs, effect/trigger/persistence, static text and source citations.
- `src/native_shape_builder.py`: python-pptx native shapes, curves where reliably supported, fall back to SVG/native line elements as needed.
- `src/effect_backend_aspose.py`: **optional** effect backend; use exact installed API, licensing check and round-trip.
- `src/effect_backend_ooxml.py`: **optional, experimental** strict XML animation backend.
- `src/qa_geometry.py`, `src/qa_science.py`, `src/qa_animation.py`: separate physics, math, visual and timing gates.
- `tests/`: positive/negative fixtures, object-ID determinism, arrow-angle checks, no unintended colors, freeze-string identity, animation group count, no phantom empirical claims.
- `build/`: diagram SVG, PNG preview, PPTX, PDF, static click-through PPTX, final contact sheet and QA reports.

**Do not merge or install this specification into production without accepted tests and source comparison.** Preserve the canonical old skill and decks as immutable audit inputs.

## 13. References

Source documentation and feature support are recorded with dated links and capability boundaries in `references/OFFICIAL_SOURCE_REGISTRY.md`. The repo's canonical sources govern *scientific claims*; vendor docs govern *software capability*. Do not cite Microsoft product guidance as proof of a P↔T_e heat mechanism.

## 14. Future maintenance

When a new presentation tool, API or PowerPoint build appears, check capability against official documentation; create a minimum example; test with actual binary on supported target platforms; update compatibility matrix, QA and example only after passing. Regenerate affected slides from the unchanged source, record version hashes and a changelog. Never promote a prototype to a verified capability based solely on a screenshot or a successful static export.
